## Overview
First dot case: no oriented edges or corners, just two adjacent bars forming an L in the front-left quadrant.

## Recognition
- Top face shows only the center sticker; every other sticker points sideways.
- Front and left faces each display a 2×1 yellow bar meeting at the FL corner.
- Back/right faces stay dark, separating it from [OLL-2](deddal://case/OLL-2).

## Technique
1. Run the classic double-sledge `(R U2 R') (R' F R F')`.
2. Repeat `U2 (R' F R F')` to finish orienting all stickers.
3. Apply AUF only if the cross needs realignment.

## Fingertricks
- Treat each `R' F R F'` as a mini packet; anchor your thumb on the front face for stability.
- Keep the right wrist steady so the `U2` transitions stay smooth.

## Common Mistakes
- Forgetting the second packet, leaving the dot pattern partially solved.
- Over-rotating the cube when a simple AUF would finish the layer.

## Practice
- Drill the two-packet rhythm slowly, then push toward sub‑1.2s solves.
- Alternate with OLL-2 to internalize the visual differences between adjacent vs. opposite bars.

## Related Cases
- [OLL-2](deddal://case/OLL-2) – Same dot but with bars on opposite sides.
- [OLL-3](deddal://case/OLL-3) – Dot case featuring diagonal headlights.

## Pro Tips
- Because every sticker is misoriented, plan your PLL while executing the second packet—the cube’s orientation never changes.

- Keep the `(R U R' U')` packet identical to your Sune muscle memory.

- Forgetting the wide-move portion and ending with a half-solved dot.
- Letting the cube wobble during `f/f'`, which slows down the final AUF.

- Alternate between this alg and OLL-1 to get comfortable switching from adjacent to opposite bars.
- Aim for consistent sub‑1.3s execution once recognition is instant.
